statements.text: Our laws need to keep up with technology. The landscape of possibilities presented by artificial intelligence is changing rapidly. We must prioritize the rights of victims first, and protect women and children from new forms of violations and punish perpetrators for their actions.
statements.venue: Press release, CA Senate District 10, on SB 926 passing Public Safety Committee

statements.text: My AI Safety Package consists of common-sense solutions to protect women and children from digital exploitation. [...] We must ensure we are working with, encouraging, and requiring tech companies to add necessary guardrails that protect vulnerable populations on the internet.
statements.venue: Press release, CA Senate District 10, on SB 1381 and AI Safety Package signed into law

statements.text: Technology evolves at a faster pace than we can legislate, and an AI moratorium would have stifled California’s ability to establish necessary oversight of AI and all the technologies it is embedded in.
statements.venue: Statement reported by NOTUS on the federal AI state-law moratorium being stripped from the reconciliation bill

statements.text: Policy doesn't move as fast as technology, and we are seeing technology that could be utilized for a lot of good also be utilized to make things more expensive for the average person.
statements.venue: ABC7 San Francisco interview on AI/dynamic pricing bill

statements.text:
Proud to join Congressman Sam Liccardo and Mayor Matt Mahan at the #GovAI Summit — discussing how California can lead on AI with innovation, accountability, and fairness. 
I’m proud of work that shapes tech policy that works for people. 
#CaliforniaLeadership #FutureOfWork https://t.co/3gmzzVDLyV
When we’re talking about moratoriums, I think that’s the wrong move. [...] And the reason for that is because you can’t stop technology.
statements.venue: CA-14 candidate debate on data centers, reported by KTVU

statements.text: Our utilities companies are not going to prioritize the infrastructure improvements that they need to do, which is something that we have been having challenges with. And AI is the literal industrial revolution to all industries that we are talking about. And I think that there is a balancing act that we need to ensure when we are talking about a roadmap for both AI and data centers.
statements.venue: CA-14 candidate debate (Dublin Chamber of Commerce), reported by NBC Bay Area
